channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar holds early June high
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is holding near the top of its recent range against the US Dollar (USD), sitting in the mid-0.5900s at the time of writing after touching its best level since early June.

item.title: Japanese Yen slips as firmer yields lift US Dollar ahead of global PMIs
item.description: USD/JPY trades north of the 159.00 barrier at the time of writing on Thursday, higher on the day and clawing back most of the previous session's losses. The move owes more to a steadier US Dollar (USD) than to anything out of Japan, with the Greenback recovering after slipping to a three-month low.

item.title: Mexican Peso holds firm as Banxico minutes supports the Peso
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) holds firm versus the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday as the Bank of Mexico (Banxico) adopted a cautious stance regarding monetary policy, while jobs data in the US showed that the labor market is stable.

item.title: South Korean Won: Rally accelerates with foreign inflows – DBS
item.description: DBS strategist Chang Wei Liang reports that South Korean Won (KRW) strength has resumed, with USD/KRW dropping to the mid-1380s even as KOSPI fell nearly 6% on semiconductor-led losses.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar firms ahead of global flash PMIs
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) is hovering near 98.90, still short of 100.00, but grinding higher on Thursday. Hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve Bank of St.

item.title: The Dollar Index takes its floor from a Fed non-voter
item.description: The Dollar Index has spent Thursday building a floor just above 98.50 and defending it with everything the calendar had to offer, and the entire effort is worth roughly a tenth of a point.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Softer Dollar offers limited relief – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) should find some relief from a softer Dollar and lower long-end US yields, with BI keeping its policy rate at 5.75% and focusing on currency stability.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Upside risk stays in focus against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD extended its overnight slide as the US Dollar (USD) sell-off pushed the pair back toward the 1.27 area.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD tests 100-day SMA as rally extends
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price extended its gains on Thursday, up more than 1.70%, even as US yields recovered some ground following the US Treasury bond buyback announcement. The XAG/USD pair trades at $68.18 at the time of writing, its highest level since June 18.

item.title: Japanese Yen underperforms as elevated Oil prices weigh, US Dollar recovers
item.description: USD/JPY rebounds on Thursday, recovering most of the previous day’s losses as the US Dollar (USD) stages a modest recovery after falling to a three-month low. At the time of writing, USD/JPY trades around 159.05, up roughly 0.55% on the day.

item.title: Gold pulls back as US yields recover after Treasury buyback
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price retreats about 0.33% on Thursday as US Treasury yields trim some of their Wednesday losses, weighing on bullion, which is also pressured by the recovery of the US Dollar. The XAU/USD pair trades at $4,509, after hitting a daily high of $4,540.

item.title: Banxico minutes signal long rate pause as inflation eases
item.description: The minutes of the Bank of Mexico (Banxico) August meeting showed that the central bank is expected to hold rates steady for some time, despite the resumption of the disinflation process.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rises as RBNZ rate hike expectations strengthen
item.description: NZD/USD advances for the second consecutive day on Thursday, trading around 0.5940 at the time of writing, up 0.12% on the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds near highs as mixed data keeps RBA tightening bets alive
item.description: AUD/USD is trading in the 0.7100 neighborhood at the time of writing on Thursday, holding close to multi-week highs after a steady climb off its earlier lows. The pair is marginally weaker on the day as the US Dollar (USD) regains a little ground, but the broader uptrend remains intact.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average sells the best outlook since 1983
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades near 53,050, more than 400 points lower on the session, after two of the strongest American data points of the month arrived in the same 12:30 GMT block and were sold on delivery.

item.title: Gold reclaims $4,500 despite rebound in US Treasury yields and US Dollar
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trims its earlier intraday losses during American trading hours on Thursday and climbs back above the $4,500 mark, even as US Treasury yields rebound and the US Dollar (USD) stabilizes following the previous day’s sharp pullback.

item.title: British Pound climbs as UK inflation keeps BoE hike bets alive
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) advances on Thursday during the North American session, up 0.25% after US economic data showed that the labor market remains solid, despite a weaker Nonfarm Payrolls in July.

item.title: Fed's Musalem: Hiking rates now could save more aggressive action later
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem is crossing the wires with remarks on the economy and the monetary policy outlook, speaking in an interview with CNBC on Thursday.

item.title: US Dollar: Debasement worries weigh after buyback – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the US Dollar (USD) is extending losses to its weakest level since mid-June as markets react to the US Treasury’s decision to double bond buybacks.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Attempts to reclaim 0.8000 after defending the 100-day SMA
item.description: USD/CHF regains ground on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) stabilises following the previous day’s broad weakness, which pushed the pair below the 0.8000 psychological mark and to its lowest level since June 17, weakening the near-term bullish structure.

item.title: Bessent wants bigger bond buybacks, but markets barely blink
item.description: United States (US) Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Thursday that the Treasury could increase bond buybacks beyond $4 billion, partly to signal that current yields do not reflect underlying economic fundamentals. He stressed that interest rates have nothing to do with the buyback decision.

item.title: WTI hits three-week high as Iran deadlock supports Oil
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil rises 1.89% on Thursday and trades around $85.85 at the time of writing, after reaching a fresh three-week high at $87.38 earlier in the day.

item.title: Indonesia: Rupiah stability supports BI pause – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Radhika Rao notes Bank Indonesia (BI) kept its policy rate at 5.75% with Acting Governor Destry maintaining a neutral bias while flagging global risks. A strong domestic growth print and Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) stability underpin the decision.

item.title: Canadian Dollar remains supported by rising Oil prices and US tariff pause
item.description: USD/CAD remains under pressure on Thursday even as the US Dollar (USD) stages a modest recovery following the previous day’s sharp selloff. Higher Oil prices support the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD), keeping the pair near a three-month low.

item.title: British Pound: Sustained break above 1.3650 may open 1.41 – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note that GBP/USD gains into the mid-1.36s are driven more by US Dollar (USD) weakness than intrinsic British Pound (GBP) strength, though United Kingdom (UK) survey data show improving manufacturing orders and pricing power.

item.title: EUR/GBP eases from intraday highs as traders eye dual flash PMIs
item.description: EUR/GBP trades near the 0.8560s zone, having drifted steadily lower from near the 0.8585 area after failing to hold its push higher. The cross is down 0.15% in Thursday's American session with traders squaring up ahead of a data-heavy Friday.

item.title: South Korean Won: Leads Asia FX on tech support – MUFG
item.description: Lloyd Chan at MUFG highlights that the Korean Won has outperformed regional peers, helped by a softer Dollar and a resilient semiconductor and AI investment cycle supporting exports and inflows.

item.title: Swedish Krona: Riksbank keeps hikes on table – BNY
item.description: BNY Mellon’s Geoff Yu reports the Swedish Riksbank left its policy rate at 1.75%, judging the stance well balanced amid stronger growth and inflation but a softer labor market. Underlying inflation is near 2% and summer readings beat forecasts.

item.title: Euro: Bullish trend eyes upper 1.17s against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report that EUR/USD gains are being driven mainly by broad US Dollar (USD) weakness, with front-end spreads narrowing since late June and supporting Euro (EUR) fundamentals.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: BI pause keeps tightening risk alive – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Moses Lim highlights that Bank Indonesia left the BI Rate at 5.75%, balancing inflation, growth and IDR stability after earlier hikes. BI has expanded hedging incentives and CNY clearing to support inflows and FX stability, while keeping SRBI yields from rising further.
